title: stream session reconciliation + keepalive heartbeat for resilient streaming (OpenAI compatibility)
author: Maya Gupta
description:
Problem and motivation: production customers running long-lived streaming sessions observed hard disconnects that led to duplicated tool/function calls or lost in-flight invocations when clients briefly lost connectivity. Existing resume semantics were insufficient for two classes of failures: short TCP disconnects and client-initiated cancels that arrive after a reconnect. This PR implements a session reconciliation + keepalive heartbeat protocol compatible with the OpenAI-style streaming API and extends the compatibility layer so that existing SDKs can opt-in without protocol churn.

Summary of changes (single-string description): Adds a per-stream session identifier (session_id) and server-issued resume_token; implements an opt-in keepalive heartbeat event that clients may send to prevent server idle timeouts; introduces server-side idle_timeout_ms and an improved resume handshake for reconciling in-flight function/tool calls. The OpenAI compatibility adapter now accepts X-Resume-Token and maps legacy cancel semantics to idempotent cancel tokens. When a client reconnects with a valid resume_token the server performs session reconciliation: it replays last sent tokens/events, re-attaches the KV cache pointer for the session, and, if a function call was in-flight, returns a single "tool_call_resume" structured event with the preserved call payload rather than reissuing the tool invocation. The design avoids duplicate side effects while preserving deterministic, observable operator behavior.

Key protocol fields and behavior: 1) session_id (client-generated UUID allowed; server validates). 2) resume_token (server-generated opaque string returned on disconnect/heartbeat interval). 3) keepalive_ping (client -> server minimal event to reset idle timer). 4) idle_timeout_ms (server config, default 45000). 5) cancel_token (idempotent cancel scope tied to session_id). 6) tool_call_resume event (server -> client) used instead of re-executing external tools on resume.

Examples: HTTP streaming connection and resume headers: "POST /v1/streams?session_id=<uuid>" with header "X-Resume-Token: <token>" on reconnect. Keepalive payload: {"type":"keepalive_ping"} sent as a short JSON event when no activity is expected.

Implementation notes: - Serving runtime: attach lightweight session metadata to in-flight request state; persist minimal reconciliation record (last 2 events, tool-call context, KV cache pointer) in the per-session store for the configured resume window. Records are stored in memory for Hosted, persisted to the Dedicated metadata store for Dedicated, and to the Private local session store for Private. - Compatibility layer: map OpenAI streaming delta events to the new internal event types; accept both X-Resume-Token and Resume-Token headers. - Function/tool calling: add call-state serialization; on reconnect the server emits tool_call_resume with the serialized args and a resume_hint flag instead of re-invoking external tool endpoints. - Security: resume_token is opaque and short-lived; rotate tokens when session_id changes or after a full cancellation. - Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless client sends session_id or keepalive_ping; OpenAI adapter accepts new headers but will not require them.

Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests added for resume handshake, duplicate-tool-call avoidance, and keepalive behavior. CI surfaced one flaky websocket close test that we fixed by increasing a test timeout. Staged rollout: feature gated via runtime flag (off by default for older deployments), enabled for API layer in Canary for 48h, then rolled to production.

Migration notes for integrators: - Short-term: clients can opt-in by generating a session_id and sending keepalive pings periodically; server will return resume_token on disconnect. - SDKs: this PR includes an opt-in flag in the TypeScript and Python SDKs (enableSessionResume) with example usage. - Operators: recommended to set idle_timeout_ms conservatively; customers using Dedicated should store session persistence to the Dedicated metadata store to allow longer resume windows.

Related: ENG-3421 (resume protocol spec), ENG-3499 (function-call idempotency), SUP-1782 (customer incident reference).
commits: feat(stream): add session_id + resume_token lifecycle (session store + reconcile)
feat(api): accept X-Resume-Token header in openai-compat adapter
chore(sdk): add enableSessionResume flag to TS/Python SDK examples
fix(test): increase websocket close timeout to prevent flaky failure
docs: document keepalive_ping and migration guidance
review_comments: Samir Khan: Can we make resume_token shorter-lived by default? Concern: long-lived tokens leak risk. Response: token TTL is configurable per deployment; default set to 5 minutes to balance reliability and security.

Elena Ruiz: How do we guarantee no duplicate tool side-effects on resume? Response: we serialize tool-call state and emit tool_call_resume; external tool providers should implement idempotency too. Added test that ensures tool endpoint not invoked twice on reconnect.
Jonas Becker: Suggest moving keepalive default into runtime config and make it tunable per-customer. Action: done; added runtime flag and operator note in docs.
Samir Khan: CI flake observed—why did websocket test fail intermittently? Response: test timing was tight; increased test timeout and added an explicit close handshake in test harness.
release_notes: Added opt-in streaming session reconciliation and keepalive heartbeat. New headers: X-Resume-Token. SDKs expose enableSessionResume flag. Default behavior unchanged for clients that do not opt-in.
